commonMistakes: Lower back rounding at the bottom of the rep
Knees caving inward on the way up
cues: Whole foot pressed into the floor
instructions: Hold a dumbbell or kettlebell vertically at chest height, elbows tucked under the weight.
Stand with feet slightly wider than shoulder-width, toes turned out 15-30 degrees.
Push your hips back and bend your knees, keeping your chest tall and the weight close to your body.
Descend until your elbows touch the insides of your knees, or as deep as you can without your lower back rounding.
Drive through your whole foot to stand, squeezing your glutes at the top.
longevityNotes: The squat pattern is how you sit, stand, and get off the floor for the rest of your life — train it for depth and control, not maximal load. A deep, easy goblet squat you can still do at 80 beats a heavy barbell you abandon at 50. Keep 2-3 reps in reserve; joint-friendly volume beats grinding singles for healthspan.
name: Goblet Squat

progression.loadingGuidance: Add 2-4 kg when you can complete 3 sets of 12 with clean form at RPE 7 or less.
progression.regressTo: Bodyweight box squat to a chair or bench

safetyNotes: If you have a knee replacement or acute knee pain, limit depth to your pain-free range and check with your clinician first. Never bounce out of the bottom position.
